summary: TechCrunch's The Interchange newsletter profiles Atlanta-based Rainforest, a 2022-founded startup that helps software companies embed payments and is positioned as a rival to Stripe, Fiserv and FIS after an $8.5 million seed round led by Accel. It also covers a class action lawsuit against PayPal over anti-steering rules, Bolt's move past an SEC probe, and a roundup of fintech news, layoffs, and funding deals.
one_line: The Interchange newsletter spotlights Rainforest, an Atlanta payments startup challenging Stripe, plus the PayPal antitrust suit, Bolt's SEC probe outcome, and weekly fintech news.
key_facts: Rainforest is an Atlanta-based startup, founded in 2022, that helps software companies embed financial services and payments into their platforms.
Accel led Rainforest's $8.5 million seed round, with Infinity Ventures, BoxGroup, The Fintech Fund, Tech Square Ventures, and Ardent Venture Partners participating.
Rainforest has secured client commitments representing more than $500 million in processing, with much of the volume guaranteed.

Rainforest CEO and co-founder Joshua Silver disagreed with a16z's Angela Strange's 2019 claim that every company would become a fintech, arguing most software companies don't want regulatory and compliance burdens.

On October 5, PayPal was hit with a class action lawsuit by consumers represented by Hagens Berman alleging its anti-steering rules stifle competition against lower-cost platforms like Stripe and Shopify.
Visa and Mastercard agreed in 2010 to eliminate similar anti-steering rules as part of a settlement after the Justice Department sued them for antitrust violations.
Bolt and co-founder Ryan Breslow were subpoenaed by the SEC over fundraising in 2021, when Bolt sought a $355 million Series E that valued it at $11 billion.
The SEC probe of Bolt took about 15 months and became public in July 2023; on August 23 the SEC said it was not recommending an enforcement action.
Banking-as-a-service startup Synapse laid off 86 people, about 40% of the company, after cutting 18% of its workforce in June.
Visa plans to invest $100 million in companies developing generative AI technologies and applications, according to Visa Ventures head David Roff.
Indian fintech Slice is merging with North East Small Finance Bank after central bank approval.
CRED grew its operating revenue 255% to $168.1 million in the financial year ending March.
Ramp ranked No. 1 on LinkedIn's top startups of 2023 list, with Synctera No. 11, Esusu No. 13, Sardine No. 16, and Tapcheck No. 48.
Stampli announced a $61M round led by Blackstone, and Brite raised $60M.
